preconditions.expression: len(good_letters) >= 1 and len(good_letters) <= 26 and all(c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in good_letters) and len(set(good_letters)) == len(good_letters)
preconditions.description: The first line contains a string of distinct lowercase English letters (good letters) with length between 1 and 26.

preconditions.expression: 1 <= len(pattern) <= 10**5 and all(c.islower() or c in {'?', '*'} for c in pattern) and pattern.count('*') <= 1
preconditions.description: The second line contains a pattern string of length between 1 and 10^5, consisting of lowercase letters, '?', and '*', with at most one '*' character.
The third line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the number of query strings.

preconditions.expression: all(len(query) >= 1 and all(c.islower() for c in query) for query in queries)
preconditions.description: Each of the n query strings is a non-empty string of lowercase English letters.
The total length of all query strings does not exceed 10^5.

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == n and all(line in {'YES', 'NO'} for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly n lines, each containing either 'YES' or 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i] == 'YES') == matches_pattern(queries[i], good_letters, pattern) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each query string, the output is 'YES' if and only if the pattern matches the query string according to the given rules: '?' can be replaced by any good letter, and '*' (if present) can be replaced by any string of bad letters (including empty).
